mainTopic: Whether משיכה (pulling an item) makes a real acquisition when a גוי is involved, shown through the ברייתא about a בן נח who steals less than a פרוטה. Then a new case where רב יוסף rules on a promise to sell land.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a proof that משיכה (pulling an item) is a real acquisition for a גוי. The proof comes from a ברייתא where a second בן נח who takes a stolen item from the first thief is also executed. Next come several sales cases. רב יוסף rules on a promise to sell land 'if I sell,' and אביי objects that no price was fixed. The גמרא then proves from a ברייתא about unloading produce that a sale is not final until the price is fixed. In the case of a promise to sell for one hundred followed by a sale to someone else for one hundred twenty, the הלכה follows רב יעקב מנהר פקוד: the extra money forced the sale, so the promise does not hold. The גמרא also rules on prices set 'as three assess' or 'as three say,' and holds that an agreed assessment stands. A new משנה follows about wine left in a funnel and about pouring wine from vessel to vessel. In its גמרא, רב הונא rules that a poured stream connects liquids for יין נסך. רב נחמן shows that the משנה in טהרות cannot be his source, and the גמרא begins a new proof from our funnel משנה, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Explaining 'not subject to restitution'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that 'לא ניתן להישבון' means the item is not under the rules of השבה at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'it is not given to be returned' mean? It means it is not under the law of returning stolen things.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains a phrase from the ברייתא about a בן נח who stole less than a פרוטה. It reads the phrase in a way that fits the idea that משיכה does not acquire for a גוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא said the stolen item 'is not given to restitution.' The גמרא reads this as saying the rules of השבה do not apply here at all, as if no real theft happened. That reading would allow us to say the pulling never made a legal transfer.

keyTerms.meaning: The smallest coin that matters in halacha
A non-Jew, bound by the seven Noahide laws

phrases.english: And what does 'it is not given to restitution' mean?
phrases.notes: This phrase comes from the ברייתא quoted just before: a בן נח who steals less than a פרוטה is executed, but the item isn't returned.

phrases.english: That it is not under the law of restitution at all.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of the ברייתא about a בן נח stealing less than a פרוטה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterpreting a phrase in the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Not given to restitution' might show that the גוי really acquired the item through משיכה.
steps.terutzMaskana: It may simply mean the rules of השבה don't apply here at all, so there is no proof of acquisition.

steps.title: The second thief in the latter clause makes no sense
steps.stepSummary: If no real acquisition happened, why is a second בן נח who takes the item from the first thief also executed?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, look at the end of the ברייתא: if his friend came and took it from him, he is executed for it. The first case is fine, because the first thief hurt the Jew. But in the second case, what did the second thief do wrong?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the reading from Step 1 by pointing to the סיפא of the same ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the רישא, the first thief can be executed because he caused the ישראל distress. In the סיפא, the second thief took the item from the first thief, not from the Jew. If the first thief never really acquired it, the second thief did nothing that counts, so why is he executed?

keyTerms.meaning: The latter clause of a teaching
The first clause of a teaching

steps.confusionAlert: The second thief is executed for taking the item from the first thief, not from the Jew. That is exactly why it is hard: he never caused the Jew any distress.

phrases.english: If so, say the latter clause:
If his fellow came and took it from him —
phrases.notes: 'His fellow' means another בן נח, who took the stolen item from the first thief.

phrases.english: he is executed for it.
Granted, the first clause makes sense,
because he caused distress to the Jew,
but in the latter clause, what did he do?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading offered in Step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the item is not under the rules of השבה at all, meaning no real acquisition happened.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the first thief never acquired the item, the second thief took nothing legally meaningful and hurt no Jew. So executing him makes no sense.

steps.title: Conclusion: pulling acquires for a non-Jew
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא concludes that משיכה בגוי קונה, and confirms it.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, learn from this: pulling acquires for a non-Jew. Learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: Because the סיפא only works if the first thief truly acquired the item, the גמרא concludes that משיכה works for a גוי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the first thief acquired the item by pulling it, then the second thief stole something that really belonged to the first thief, so he is liable. This settles the question the סוגיא has been asking about משיכה with a גוי.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it / conclude from this
Pulling an object toward oneself, a way of acquiring movable items

steps.whatToRemember: משיכה בגוי קונה: pulling an item is a real acquisition for a גוי. The proof is that a second בן נח who takes the item from the first thief is executed, which shows the first thief really owned it.

phrases.english: Rather, learn from it:
pulling acquires for a non-Jew,
learn from it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of Step 2 by dropping the reading of Step 1.

steps.title: A promise to sell land, then a sale to someone else
steps.stepSummary: A man promised to sell his land to his friend if he ever sold it, then sold it to another person. רב יוסף rules the first man acquires.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man said to his friend: 'If I sell this land, I will sell it to you.' He went and sold it to another person. רב יוסף said: the first one acquired it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic with a story and רב יוסף's ruling about a promise to sell land.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The owner did not sell the land to his friend. He only promised that any future sale would go to him. רב יוסף still rules that the friend, the first one, has the right to the land over the later buyer.

phrases.english: A certain man said to his fellow:
'If I sell this land —
I will sell it to you,'
he went and sold it to another person,
Rav Yosef said: The first one acquired it.
phrases.notes: 'The first one' is the friend who was promised the land, not the person who actually bought it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic, separate from the משיכה discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When someone promises 'if I sell, I'll sell to you' and then sells to another, the first, promised party acquires the land.

steps.title: אביי objects that no price was fixed
steps.stepSummary: אביי challenges רב יוסף's ruling: the friend cannot acquire, because no price was ever fixed.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to רב יוסף: But he never fixed a price!
steps.whatsHappening: אביי attacks רב יוסף's ruling from Step 4. In that case nobody ever agreed on a price, so how can the friend acquire the land?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יוסף said the first friend acquires the land. אביי points to a missing piece: a sale needs an agreed price (פסיקת דמים). Without one, there seems to be no sale at all.

keyTerms.meaning: He fixed the price, settling the exact sum
אביי, the student of רב יוסף, who raises the challenge

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
phrases.notes: "Him" is רב יוסף, whose ruling we saw in the last step.

phrases.english: But he did not fix a price!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אַבָּיֵי: וְהָא לָא פְּסַק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יוסף's ruling from Step 4.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יוסף's ruling that the first friend acquires the land.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: No price was fixed, and a sale without a fixed price does not take effect.

steps.title: אביי's proof from selling wine to a gentile
steps.stepSummary: אביי proves from a משנה that a sale only takes effect once the price is fixed.
steps.simpleTranslation: How do we know that whenever no price was fixed there is no acquisition? From the משנה: if someone sells his wine to a gentile and fixed the price before measuring, the money is permitted. If he measured before fixing the price, the money is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי backs up his challenge with a source. He brings a משנה about a Jew selling wine to a נכרי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the wine is poured into the gentile's container, it becomes forbidden as יין נסך. If the money is forbidden when the price was fixed afterwards, then the sale only happened at the price-fixing, when the wine was already forbidden. So a sale needs a fixed price.

keyTerms.meaning: And from where do you say this? (asks for the source)
He measured the wine out into the buyer's container
Its money: the payment for the wine

phrases.english: And from where do you say

phrases.aramaic: דְּכֹל הֵיכָא דְּלָא פְּסַק לָא קְנָה?
phrases.english: that wherever he did not fix a price, he has not acquired?
As we learned in a mishna:
One who sells his wine to a gentile,
if he fixed the price before he measured,
phrases.notes: Measuring here means pouring the wine into the gentile's container. That pouring is what makes it forbidden wine.

phrases.english: the money for it is permitted;
if he measured before he fixed the price,
the money for it is forbidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמְנָא תֵּימְרָא דְּכֹל הֵיכָא דְּלָא פְּסַק לָא קְנָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supplies the source for אביי's challenge.
steps.raayaObject: A sale does not take effect until a price is fixed.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה about selling wine to a נכרי: the money is forbidden if the wine was measured before the price was fixed.

steps.title: What is the final ruling?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the final conclusion is on this question.
steps.simpleTranslation: What was concluded about this?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what the final הלכה is: does a sale need a fixed price or not? This question sets up the next few moves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי has given a proof, but the גמרא is not ready to treat the matter as closed. It asks for the bottom line.

keyTerms.meaning: What was decided about it? (asks for the final ruling)

phrases.english: What was concluded about this?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks whether אביי's proof settles the matter.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a sale takes effect without a fixed price.

steps.title: Why ask? We already said it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא wonders why the question was asked at all, since אביי's proof seems to answer it.
steps.simpleTranslation: What do you mean, "what was concluded"? It is as we said!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on its own question. אביי already proved from the משנה that a price must be fixed, so why ask again?
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line treats the matter as already decided by the wine משנה. It gets the next step ready, where the גמרא explains why the proof is not enough.

phrases.english: What do you mean, "what was concluded about this"?!
It is as we have stated!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions why Step 7's question was needed.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The answer seems to be what אביי already proved: no fixed price means no sale.

steps.title: Maybe forbidden wine is a special case
steps.stepSummary: The proof may not work: the wine case could be stricter only because יין נסך is a severe prohibition.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps the strictness of libation wine makes it different.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why it asked. The wine משנה might not teach a general rule about sales.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Perhaps the money is forbidden only because the rabbis were extra strict about יין נסך. In that case it tells us nothing about ordinary buying and selling. So אביי's proof is weakened, and a better source is needed.

keyTerms.meaning: Wine used (or likely used) for idol worship; forbidden even for benefit

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying אביי is wrong. It only says his proof from wine might not apply to regular sales.

phrases.english: Perhaps the strictness of libation wine is different.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the question in Step 7 by weakening the proof in Step 6.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the proof only, not אביי's position itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: The wine case may reflect a special strictness of יין נסך rather than a general rule about sales.

steps.title: רב הונא's case: the produce was brought in but not unloaded
steps.stepSummary: A new proof from רב הונא's ruling, based on a ברייתא: if the buyer only led the seller's loaded donkeys into his house, nobody has acquired, whether or not a price was fixed.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: Rav Idi bar Avin said that a case came before רב חסדא, who brought it to רב הונא. רב הונא resolved it from a ברייתא: if the buyer led the seller's donkey drivers and workers into his house, then whether the price was fixed before measuring or the measuring came before the price, he has not acquired. Either side can back out.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a stronger proof from an ordinary sale of produce, with no forbidden wine involved. This first part of the ברייתא sets up the key contrast that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the produce is still on the seller's donkeys and workers, so no real act of acquisition happened. That is why nobody acquires, even if a price was fixed. This is the background for the next clause.

keyTerms.meaning: His donkey drivers and his workers
To back out of the deal

phrases.english: Come and hear,
as Rav Idi bar Avin said:
There was a case in the study hall of Rav Chisda,
and Rav Chisda brought it to the study hall of Rav Huna,
and he resolved it from what we learned:
If he drew the seller's donkey drivers and workers
phrases.notes: The produce is still loaded on the seller's donkeys and workers. The buyer just led them in.

phrases.english: and brought them into his house,
whether he fixed the price before he measured
or he measured before he fixed the price,
he has not acquired,
and both of them can back out.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע, דְּאָמַר רַב אִידִי בַּר אָבִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the weakened wine proof with a proof from an ordinary sale.
steps.raayaObject: A sale does not take effect until a price is fixed.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא relied on by רב הונא.

steps.title: Even after unloading, a sale needs a fixed price
steps.stepSummary: If the buyer unloaded the produce into his house, the deal holds only if the price was fixed first. Otherwise either side can still back out.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he unloaded the produce and brought it into his house: if the price was fixed before measuring, neither side can back out. If he measured before fixing the price, both can back out.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the key clause of the proof. Unloading is a real act of acquisition, yet the sale still depends on whether a price was fixed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The act of acquisition is identical in both cases. The only difference is whether a price was fixed. This shows, in an ordinary sale, that no fixed price means no binding sale, which supports אביי.
steps.whatToRemember: An act of acquisition alone is not enough. Until the price is fixed, either side may back out. This supports אביי against רב יוסף.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets the general rule that a sale needs both an act of acquisition and an agreed price.

phrases.english: If he unloaded them and brought them into his house,
if he fixed the price before he measured,
neither of them can back out;
if he measured before he fixed the price,
both of them can back out.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא begun in Step 10 with its decisive clause.
steps.raayaObject: Even with a valid act of acquisition, the sale is not final until the price is fixed.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The second clause of the ברייתא: produce unloaded into the buyer's house.

steps.title: A promise to sell land for one hundred, then a sale for one hundred twenty
steps.stepSummary: A man promised his friend: if I sell this land, I will sell it to you for 100. He then sold it to someone else for 120. רב כהנא rules that the first man acquires it.
steps.simpleTranslation: A certain man told his friend: 'If I sell this land, I will sell it to you for one hundred זוזים.' He then went and sold it to someone else for one hundred and twenty. רב כהנא said: the first one acquires it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a real-life sales case and gives רב כהנא's ruling on it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The seller made a promise that only applies 'if I sell.' Once he did sell, רב כהנא holds the promise kicks in, so the friend gets the land at 100.

phrases.english: A certain man who said to his friend:
"If I sell this land,
I will sell it to you for one hundred זוזים,"
he went and sold it to another person
for one hundred and twenty.
רב כהנא said: The first one has acquired it.
phrases.notes: He means the friend who got the promise gets the land, at the promised price of one hundred.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new sales case after the discussion of when a buyer acquires before the price is fixed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב כהנא: the first person who got the promise acquires the land.

steps.title: The extra money forced his hand
steps.stepSummary: רב יעקב מנהר פקוד objects: the extra twenty זוזים is what made him sell, so the promise to sell at 100 never really came into play.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יעקב from נהר פקוד challenged this: Those extra זוזים pushed him to sell!
steps.whatsHappening: רב יעקב מנהר פקוד attacks רב כהנא's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The promise was about a sale he would make freely at 100. But he only sold because someone offered 120, so the money pushed him into it. That is not the sale he promised, so the first buyer gets nothing.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב יַעֲקֹב מִנְּהַר פְּקוֹד:
phrases.english: רב יעקב of נהר פקוד objected to this:
Those coins forced him!
phrases.notes: He means the extra twenty. Without that higher offer he wouldn't have sold at all.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב יַעֲקֹב מִנְּהַר פְּקוֹד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב כהנא's ruling in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב כהנא's ruling that the first buyer acquires.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The promise was for a free sale. This sale happened only because of a higher price, so the promise does not apply.

steps.title: The ruling follows רב יעקב מנהר פקוד
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה follows רב יעקב מנהר פקוד: the first buyer does not get the land.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה follows רב יעקב from נהר פקוד.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא decides the case in favor of the objector.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second buyer, who paid 120, keeps the land. A promise of 'if I sell' does not hold the seller to a lower price once a higher offer is what made him sell.
steps.whatToRemember: 'If I sell, I'll sell to you for 100' does not hold when the seller sold only because of a higher offer. The הלכה follows רב יעקב מנהר פקוד.

phrases.english: And the הלכה is like רב יעקב of נהר פקוד.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides between רב כהנא and רב יעקב מנהר פקוד.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The first buyer does not acquire. The sale for 120 stands.

steps.title: A price set 'as three assess' or 'as three say'
steps.stepSummary: If he said 'as three assess,' two of the three are enough. If he said 'as three say,' all three must agree.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he said to him 'as three assess it,' even two out of the three is enough. If he said 'as three say,' it is not set until all three say it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new rule about prices set by outside assessors, and shows how the exact wording matters.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Assess' points to an assessment process, where a majority of the three decides. 'Say' points to what is actually said, so he needs all three to say the same price.
steps.confusionAlert: The two phrases sound almost the same, but they lead to different rules. 'Assess' needs only a majority. 'Say' needs everyone.

phrases.english: If he said to him, "As three assess it,"
even two out of the three is enough.
"As three say,"
not until all three say it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new sales rule, about setting a price through outside assessors.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'Assessed by three' means a majority is enough. 'Said by three' needs all three.

steps.title: A price set by four needs all four
steps.stepSummary: If he said 'as four assess,' all four must agree. All the more so if he said 'as four say.'
steps.simpleTranslation: If he said 'as four assess,' it is not set until all four say it. All the more so where he said 'as four say.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא carries the wording rule over to a group of four.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With four, even the word 'assess' needs all of them. Asking for four shows he wanted more than an ordinary three-person assessment. 'Say' is even stronger, so it surely needs all four.
steps.whatToRemember: Three 'assess': majority. Three 'say': all three. Four, with either word: all four.

phrases.english: "As four assess it,"
not until all four say it,
and all the more so where
he said to him, "As four say."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Carries the rule from step 15 over to four assessors.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: With four assessors, all four must agree, whichever word he used.

steps.title: Can one side demand three better assessors?
steps.stepSummary: After three assessed the item, the other side asked for three more expert assessors. רב פפא rules that he can hold up the deal.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him 'as three assess it,' and three came and assessed it. Then the other one said: 'Let three others come who know better!' רב פפא said: By law, he can hold it up.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new case: one side wants to replace the assessors. רב פפא gives his ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The worry is that more expert assessors would set a more accurate price. רב פפא lets the objecting side block the price until better experts come.

keyTerms.meaning: they know better, are more expert
that he can hold it up, block it

phrases.english: He said to him: "As three assess it,"
and three came and assessed it,
and the other one said:
Let three other people come
who know better!
רב פפא said:
By law, he can hold it up.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַאֲמַר לֵיהּ אִידַּךְ לֵיתוֹ תְּלָתָא אַחֲרִינֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the 'as three assess' case from step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב פפא: a side may block the price and ask for more expert assessors.

steps.title: Who says the new ones know better?
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע objects: there is no way to know the new assessors are more expert. Maybe the first ones are.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא son of רב יהושע challenged this: How do we know these new ones know better? Maybe these first ones know better!
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע attacks רב פפא's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Calling the new group 'better' is only a claim. Since we cannot be sure, there is no reason to throw out the first assessment, which was done exactly as agreed.

phrases.aramaic: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: רב הונא son of רב יהושע objected to this:
From where do we know that those new ones know better?
Perhaps these first ones know better!

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְקֵיף לַהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב פפא's ruling in step 17.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's ruling that a side may block the price.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Nobody can prove the new assessors are better, so the agreed assessment should stand.

steps.title: The ruling follows רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע
steps.stepSummary: The הלכה follows רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע: the first three assessors' price stands.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the הלכה follows רב הונא son of רב יהושע.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles the dispute and ends the section on business deals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the agreed assessors set the price, neither side can push it off by asking for 'better' experts.
steps.whatToRemember: An agreed assessment by three stands. One side cannot demand new 'more expert' assessors.

phrases.aramaic: וְהִלְכְתָא כְּרַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ.
phrases.english: And the הלכה is like רב הונא son of רב יהושע.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהִלְכְתָא כְּרַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Decides between רב פפא and רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The first assessment stands. No one can block it by asking for other assessors.

steps.title: משנה: wine left in a funnel
steps.stepSummary: Someone used a funnel to measure wine into a נכרי's jug and then into a Jew's jug. If wine was still left in the funnel, the Jew's wine is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: If someone took the funnel and measured wine into a נכרי's jug, and then measured wine into a Jew's jug, and wine is still sitting in the funnel, it is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins, going back to the topic of wine that becomes forbidden through a נכרי.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wine left in the funnel touched the נכרי's jug, so it counts as forbidden. When more wine flows through into the Jew's jug, that leftover mixes in and makes the Jew's wine forbidden.

phrases.english: משנה: If one took the funnel
and measured wine into a נכרי's jug,
and then measured again
into a Jew's jug,

phrases.aramaic: אִם יֵשׁ בּוֹ עַכֶּבֶת יַיִן — אָסוּר.
phrases.english: if there is leftover wine in it, it is forbidden.
phrases.notes: 'In it' means in the funnel. If wine is still stuck there from the first pouring, the Jew's wine becomes forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה, back to the laws of יין נסך.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Leftover wine in the funnel makes the Jew's wine forbidden.

steps.title: Pouring from one vessel to another
steps.stepSummary: When pouring from one vessel into another, the wine in the vessel he poured from is permitted, and the wine in the vessel he poured into is forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone pours from one vessel into another, what is left in the vessel he poured from is permitted, and what is in the vessel he poured into is forbidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives a second rule: which wine becomes forbidden when wine is poured into a vessel that makes it forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The wine still in the vessel he poured from stays permitted, and only the wine in the receiving vessel becomes forbidden. The משנה gives only the ruling, not a reason, and this seems hard to fit with רב הונא's view (Step 23) that a poured stream does connect the wine.
steps.confusionAlert: The two Hebrew phrases differ by just one word: 'from it' (מִמֶּנּוּ) versus 'into it' (לְתוֹכוֹ). The vessel he poured from is permitted, and the one he poured into is forbidden.

phrases.english: One who pours from one vessel into another vessel,
the wine in the vessel he poured from is permitted,
and the wine in the vessel he poured into is forbidden.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second rule of the same משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Pouring makes only the receiving vessel's wine forbidden. The vessel he poured from stays permitted.

steps.title: A משנה elsewhere: which flows join liquids together
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה from טהרות. A poured stream, a downhill flow, and light moisture are not a חיבור for טומאה or טהרה, but a pond is.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: We learned in another משנה: A poured stream, liquid flowing down a slope, and light moisture do not connect liquids, not for impurity and not for purity. A pond does connect them, for impurity and for purity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens by quoting a משנה from a different tractate. It is setting up the background for the discussion about יין נסך that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A 'connection' (חיבור) means two bodies of liquid count as one. A thin stream, a slope-flow, or bare moisture does not make them one for טומאה or for completing a מקוה. A pond is one solid body of liquid, so it does join them.

keyTerms.meaning: A stream of liquid being poured from one vessel into another
Moisture wet enough to make something else wet
A connection that makes two liquids count as one

phrases.english: GEMARA: We learned there:
phrases.notes: 'There' means a משנה in another tractate, טהרות.

phrases.english: A poured stream, and liquid flowing down a slope,
and liquid that is just moist enough to wet
is not a connection,
neither for impurity nor for purity.
A pond
is a connection for impurity and for purity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the new משנה, bringing in an outside משנה as background.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A poured stream, a downhill flow, and moisture are not a חיבור for טומאה or טהרה. A pond is.

steps.title: רב הונא: for libation wine these flows do connect
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא rules that a poured stream, a downhill flow, and moisture are a חיבור for יין נסך.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: A poured stream, a downhill flow, and light moisture are a connection for the laws of יין נסך.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא gives a ruling. For יין נסך, even these thin flows connect the wine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the result is the opposite of the טומאה and טהרה rule. Suppose a stream of wine touches forbidden wine. The wine it comes from becomes forbidden along with it.

keyTerms.meaning: Wine poured for idol worship, or wine forbidden because a נכרי may have used it that way
With regard to, for the matter of

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two areas. For טומאה and טהרה a stream does NOT connect, but רב הונא says that for יין נסך it DOES.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said:
A poured stream, a downhill flow, and moisture
are a connection for the matter of libation wine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the categories from the משנה and gives a ruling for יין נסך.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: For יין נסך, a poured stream, a downhill flow, and moisture all count as a חיבור.

steps.title: רב נחמן asks for רב הונא's source
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן asks רב הונא where his rule comes from. He suggests a possible source: an inference from the first half of the משנה in טהרות.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said to רב הונא: Where do you get this from? Do you mean from the משנה that says a stream, a downhill flow, and moisture do not connect for impurity or purity? You would learn from it: only for impurity and purity are they not a connection, but for יין נסך they are a connection.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן challenges רב הונא by asking for his source. He offers one possible source, so that he can test it in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The suggested proof works from what the משנה leaves out. It says 'not for impurity and not for purity,' which seems to hint that for other matters, like יין נסך, the flows do connect. This proposed proof is set up only to be knocked down.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do you know this?
If you will say, introducing a possible source
But, implying that, used to draw an inference

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן לְרַב הוּנָא:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said to Rav Huna:
From where do you have this?
If you say it is from what we learned:
A poured stream, a downhill flow, and moisture

phrases.aramaic: אֵינוֹ חִיבּוּר לֹא לְטוּמְאָה וְלֹא לְטׇהֳרָה,
phrases.english: are not a connection, neither for impurity nor for purity,

phrases.aramaic: לְטוּמְאָה וּלְטׇהֳרָה הוּא דְּלָא הָוֵי חִיבּוּר,
phrases.english: it is for impurity and purity that it is not a connection,

phrases.aramaic: הָא לְעִנְיַן יֵין נֶסֶךְ הָוֵי חִיבּוּר —
phrases.english: but for libation wine it is a connection —

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the source behind רב הונא's ruling.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's ruling that the flows are a חיבור for יין נסך
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ruling needs a source. The obvious candidate is an inference from the רישא of the משנה in טהרות, and that inference is about to be tested.

steps.title: The second half of the משנה cancels out the proof
steps.stepSummary: The סיפא about the pond leads to the opposite inference. So nothing can be learned from that משנה about יין נסך.
steps.simpleTranslation: Say the last part: A pond is a connection for impurity and purity. That suggests only for impurity and purity is it a connection, but for יין נסך it is not. Rather, nothing can be learned from this משנה.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן knocks down the proposed source. He shows that the second half of the same משנה would teach the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Reading the סיפא the same way would mean that even a pond does not connect for יין נסך. A pond is a stronger connection than a thin stream, so a stream surely would not connect either. That is the opposite of what the רישא seemed to imply. Since the two inferences cancel each other out, the משנה says nothing either way about יין נסך.

keyTerms.meaning: Say the last part of the משנה
Nothing can be learned from it

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה in טהרות cannot serve as a source for יין נסך, because its two halves would point in opposite directions. רב הונא still needs a different source.

phrases.english: Say the last clause:
A pond is a connection for impurity and for purity,
it is for impurity and purity that it is a connection,

phrases.aramaic: הָא לְעִנְיַן יֵין נֶסֶךְ לָא הָוֵי חִיבּוּר.
phrases.english: but for libation wine it is not a connection.
Rather, from this nothing can be learned.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the source suggested in the previous step.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the משנה in טהרות as a source for רב הונא. It does not reject רב הונא's ruling itself.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Reading the רישא and the סיפא the same way gives two opposite conclusions about יין נסך, so the inference cannot be trusted.

steps.title: Starting a proof from our משנה about the funnel
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a proof for רב הונא from our own משנה. Someone measured wine through a funnel into a נכרי's jug and then into a Jew's jug.
steps.simpleTranslation: We learned: If someone took the funnel and measured wine into a נכרי's jug, and then measured wine into a Jew's jug...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes our own משנה again, this time to try to prove רב הונא's rule. This step is only the setup. The proof itself continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the same funnel case from earlier, now brought in for a new purpose. The idea it is building toward: if leftover wine in the funnel can forbid the Jew's wine, maybe the poured stream itself counts as a חיבור.

keyTerms.meaning: And then went back and did it again

phrases.english: We learned: If one took the funnel
and measured into a gentile's jug,

phrases.aramaic: וְחָזַר וּמָדַד לְתוֹךְ צְלוֹחִיתוֹ שֶׁל יִשְׂרָאֵל.
phrases.english: and then measured into a Jew's jug.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the first source fails, the גמרא tries a new source for רב הונא.
steps.raayaObject: רב הונא's rule that a poured stream is a חיבור for יין נסך
steps.raayaSupportSource: Our משנה about measuring wine through a funnel into a נכרי's jug and then into a Jew's jug
